issues.failure_explanation: The derived cylindrical component uses coefficient -\pi/2, but the final Dirac form NC_delta uses +\pi (with the sign reversal in \gamma_i, giving -\pi), a factor-2 discrepancy. The real embedding further uses \pi for edges but \pi/2 for vertices, inconsistent with NC_delta. Moreover, the cited metric theorem has coefficient \pi^2/4, which would require different coefficients in the Dirac weights. The half-circle integral is also evaluated as \pi/2 \beta_T, whereas a semicircle of radius 1 has integral 2\beta_T. These inconsistencies mean the explicit Dirac decomposition is not the normal cycle and does not agree with the cited metric formula.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the half-circle and half-sphere integrals correctly, propagate the correct coefficients through the cylindrical and spherical components, and make NC_delta, the real embedding, and thm:added-1 mutually consistent.
issues.overall_effect: The Dirac delta decomposition, the real-valued embedding, and the resulting compression algorithm are not reliably connected to the normal-cycle metric. Any claimed agreement with thm:added-1 and any compression guarantee based on these weights is undermined.
issues.title: Incorrect/inconsistent coefficients in normal-cycle Dirac decomposition
issues.why_classification: The core explicit decomposition used to apply the compression algorithm is mathematically inconsistent; without resolving the coefficients, the paper's main construction does not provably represent the normal cycle.

issues.failure_explanation: The bounds are independent of the weights \alpha_i. The approximation error for a weighted sum \sum \delta_{x_i}\alpha_i is \alpha^T(K_{XX}-Q_{XX})\alpha, which scales quadratically with \|\alpha\|. For example, with an orthogonal kernel and a control set omitting one point, a target \delta_{x_2}T has error T^2 while tr(K_{XX}-Q_{XX}) is fixed, so the claimed bound fails for large T. A correct bound must include a factor such as \|\alpha\|^2 or an assumption normalizing the weights.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the bounds with a weight-dependent factor (e.g., \|\alpha\|^2 or \max_i\|\alpha_i\|^2) or explicitly normalize the target functional before applying the theorem.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical guarantee on compression error is not valid for the normal-cycle weights, which are not normalized and can be arbitrarily large with mesh scale. The advertised exponential decay and the claim that guarantees from SparseNystromCurrVar automatically carry over are unsupported.
issues.title: Compression error bounds lack dependence on target weights
issues.why_classification: The central theoretical guarantee of the paper is false as stated for arbitrary normal-cycle weights, so the main promised error control does not follow without a substantive correction.

issues.failure_explanation: Expanding \begin{pmatrix}0\\e_1\end{pmatrix}\wedge\begin{pmatrix}0\\e_2\end{pmatrix} gives coefficient a_1b_3-a_3b_1 for e_1\wedge e_3. Since u=e_1\times e_2, this coefficient equals -u_2, not +u_2. Thus the displayed expression should have a minus sign on the u_2 term. This makes the subsequent definition of \alpha_i (and the spherical Dirac weights) incorrect as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the u_2 term to -u_2 (or redefine the corresponding basis element \tilde b_2) and propagate the sign into the definition of \alpha_i.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit spherical weights are wrong by a sign in one coordinate, so the stated Dirac decomposition does not exactly represent the normal-cycle action on forms.
issues.title: Sign error in spherical component wedge expansion
issues.why_classification: The error is a single sign in one basis component and can be fixed locally; the overall compression method and metric structure are not otherwise changed.
